items.name: Chhurpi (Himalayan hard cheese)
items.prabhava: Rock-hard smoked yak/cow cheese chewed for hours in the high Himalaya — slow-release protein for cold, hard travel.
combinations: soft chhurpi cooked into soups and vegetables
items.preparation: Hard chhurpi is softened by long chewing; the soft fresh form cooks like paneer in Himalayan curries.

items.name: Yak milk
items.prabhava: Richest of the common milks — nearly twice the fat of cow milk; the high-altitude building food.
items.preparation: Always boiled and warm; its density suits the cold heights it comes from — dilute or spice at lower altitudes.

items.name: Yak butter
items.prabhava: The fuel of butter tea — high-altitude fat that answers cold, wind and dryness (the vata trinity of the mountains).
combinations: churned into salted butter tea (po cha)
contraindications: lowland sedentary use (a working fat for hard cold labor)
items.preparation: Traditional in salted tea with roasted barley flour; treat as ghee's heavier mountain cousin.

items.name: Kharvas (colostrum pudding)
items.prabhava: Steamed pudding of bovine colostrum (piyusha) — traditional strength-and-immunity delicacy given especially to children and the recovering.
combinations: steamed with jaggery, cardamom and nutmeg
contraindications: occasional availability food — never a daily item
items.preparation: First-milk colostrum steamed with sweetener until custard-set; dense building food in small squares.
provenance: Maharashtrian-Andhra tradition; piyusha in classical dairy lists

items.name: Panta bhat (fermented rice)
items.prabhava: Cooked rice soaked overnight in water — mild lacto-fermentation cools the body and feeds the gut; the farmer's summer breakfast across east and south India.
combinations: with rock salt, shallot and green chili (Bengali-Odia style)
with curd and salt (Tamil pazhaya sadam)
contraindications: ferment only overnight — longer risks spoilage
items.preparation: Cover cooked rice with water overnight at room temperature; eat next morning with salt and accompaniments.

items.name: Singhara flour halwa
items.prabhava: Fasting-day sweet of water-chestnut flour — shringataka is classically cooling and building; the vrat kitchen's grain-free halwa.
combinations: vrat meals with ghee and cardamom
items.preparation: Roast singhara flour in ghee until aromatic, add hot water and sweetener, stir to a glossy mass.
provenance: Vrat tradition; shringataka in classical lists

items.name: Gingelly oil pickle base
items.prabhava: The South Indian pickle medium — sesame oil's warmth carries and preserves; a condiment-dose agni kindler.
combinations: a spoon of pickle beside curd rice (the classic pairing)
items.preparation: Pickles are seasoning, not vegetables — a teaspoon beside the meal; til oil versions age and digest best.
provenance: South Indian achar tradition; tila taila base

items.name: Warm boiled water
items.prabhava: The simplest medicine in the pharmacopoeia — boiled, reduced water that kindles agni, melts ama and clears the channels; the default drink of Ayurvedic daily routine.
combinations: boiled down by a quarter (classical ushnodaka)
contraindications: high pitta in summer prefers room-temperature or cooled-boiled water
items.preparation: Boil water 5–10 minutes (classically until reduced by a quarter); sip warm through the day from a flask.

items.name: Copper-stored water
items.prabhava: Water stored overnight in a copper vessel — traditional morning drink credited with mild antimicrobial action; modern evidence supports small copper leaching, so moderation governs.
combinations: 1–2 glasses on waking, from an overnight-stored vessel
viruddha: storing sour liquids in copper (leaches excess copper — never lemon water in copper)
items.preparation: Store plain water overnight in a clean copper vessel; drink on waking. Wash the vessel with acid (lemon-salt) but never store acids in it.

items.name: Sugarcane juice
items.prabhava: Ikshu rasa is classically cooling, building and diuretic — the summer roadside restorative; fresh-pressed is the only real form.
combinations: fresh-pressed with lime and ginger (the classic trio)
contraindications: hygiene of the press (street stalls — drink where turnover is fast)
items.preparation: Only fresh-pressed and promptly drunk — it ferments within hours; lime and ginger brighten and lighten it.

items.name: Sweet lime water
combinations: fresh lime, water, mishri or sugar
viruddha: with milk near in time (curdling sour)
items.preparation: Fresh lime in cool (not iced) water with mishri; the gentler face of shikanji for pitta summers.

items.name: Salted lime water
items.prabhava: Lime with rock salt and roasted cumin — the electrolyte-and-agni drink; the classical answer to heat exhaustion and flat digestion alike.
combinations: rock salt and roasted cumin powder
before or with meals for weak agni
items.preparation: Fresh lime, rock salt, roasted cumin in cool water; the salted version is the digestive, the sweet version the cooler.

items.name: Jaljeera
items.prabhava: Cumin-mint-black-salt water — the pre-meal appetizer drink that wakes a dull agni and settles post-meal heaviness.
combinations: with mint, tamarind and black salt
items.preparation: Whisk roasted cumin, mint, black salt and a little tamarind or amchur into cool water; drink before meals.

items.name: Aam panna
items.prabhava: Roasted green-mango cooler with cumin and black salt — the traditional shield against loo (heat-stroke wind); sourness that cools by preserving fluids.
combinations: before midday outings in high summer
items.preparation: Roast or boil green mangoes, squeeze the pulp into water with cumin, mint, black salt and a little jaggery.
provenance: North Indian summer tradition; amra panaka lineage

items.name: Bael sherbet
items.prabhava: Ripe bael pulp whisked into water — the classical gut-soothing summer drink; bilva is the digestive tract's great friend in both loose and sluggish states.
combinations: with a little jaggery and cardamom
contraindications: constipation from ripe fruit in excess (classical note: ripe bael binds)
items.preparation: Scoop ripe pulp, soak briefly, whisk and strain into water with jaggery; drink fresh in the morning heat.

items.name: Kokum sherbet
items.prabhava: The rare sour that cools — kokum's signature; the Konkan coast's answer to summer acidity and heat.
combinations: with roasted cumin and black salt
as sol kadhi when blended with coconut milk
items.preparation: Steep dried kokum petals, press, sweeten lightly and season with cumin; ruby-pink and genuinely pitta-friendly.

items.name: Khus sherbet
items.prabhava: Ushira (vetiver root) is the classical deep-cooler — khus syrup in water carries its green coolness into the fiercest afternoons.
combinations: khus syrup in cool water or milk
items.preparation: Stir khus syrup into cool water; classically ushira was steeped as hima (cold infusion) — syrup is the modern shortcut.
provenance: Classical ushira; North Indian sherbet tradition

items.name: Rose sherbet
items.prabhava: Rose is the heart-and-pitta flower — its sherbet cools emotion and body together; the iftar and summer-wedding drink of the subcontinent.
combinations: rose syrup in cool water or milk
contraindications: choose real rose distillate over artificial essence
items.preparation: Stir rose syrup or gulkand into cool water; with milk it becomes rose milk (see separate entry).
provenance: Indo-Persian sherbet tradition; shatapatri (rose) in later nighantus

items.name: Gond katira cooler
items.prabhava: Tragacanth gum crystals soaked into cooling jelly — folk tradition's heat-stroke preventive, stirred into milk or sherbets in the hottest weeks.
combinations: soaked overnight, stirred into rose sherbet or milk
contraindications: always fully soaked with ample fluid (swells; never dry)
items.preparation: Soak a teaspoon of crystals overnight — they bloom into jelly; fold into cool drinks. Note: gond katira (cooling) is distinct from gond (acacia, heating).

items.name: Thandai
items.prabhava: The festival cooler of Holi and Shivratri — almonds, char magaz, poppy, fennel, rose, cardamom and pepper ground into milk; a complete cooling-tonic formula.
combinations: classic paste: almond, melon seeds, poppy, fennel, rose, cardamom, black pepper
contraindications: note: bhang thandai is an intoxicating variant — this entry is the plain food form only
items.preparation: Soak and grind the seed-spice paste, whisk into sweetened cool milk and strain; festival portions, not daily glasses.
provenance: North Indian festival tradition; char magaz formula

items.name: Badam milk
items.prabhava: Ground soaked almonds simmered in milk with saffron and cardamom — the classical brain-and-strength drink for students and convalescents.
combinations: warm at night for sleep and strength
items.preparation: Grind soaked, peeled almonds to paste; simmer in milk with saffron-cardamom; serve warm in winter.

items.name: Rose milk
items.prabhava: Chilled rose-syrup milk of South Indian summers — rose tempers milk's heaviness with its pitta-calming fragrance.
combinations: rose syrup in cool (not ice-cold) milk
items.preparation: Stir real rose syrup into cool boiled-and-cooled milk; room-cool rather than refrigerator-cold honors the milk rules.

items.name: Masala chai
items.prabhava: India's answer to tea's dryness — ginger, cardamom, cinnamon and clove simmered with milk turn a rough stimulant into a warming, workable daily drink.
combinations: after breakfast rather than empty stomach
items.preparation: Simmer crushed spices with tea, add milk and boil once; sweeten modestly — the spices, not the sugar, are the point.

items.name: Tulsi tea
items.prabhava: The sacred morning infusion — tulsi's warming clarity for chest, head and mood; the everyday adaptogenic cup of Indian households.
viruddha: milk in the same cup (traditional tulsi-milk caution)
items.preparation: Steep 5–10 fresh leaves or 1 tsp dried, covered, 5 minutes; honey only once drinkably warm.

items.name: Lemongrass tea
items.prabhava: Citrus-scented grass of Maharashtrian tea gardens — mildly warming, digestive and calming; often blended into chai as gavati chaha.
items.preparation: Bruise fresh blades and simmer 3–5 minutes, alone or in milk tea; strain well — the fibers are sharp.
